etymologies.etymologyHTML: Borrowed from Middle French portable, or from Latin portabilis.

definitions.definition: Able to be carried or easily moved.
Able to be transferred from one organization to another.
(computing) Of software: able to be run on multiple hardware or operating systems.

quote.citation: 2012, Herbert Schildt, C++: A Beginner's Guide, Second Edition, page 6:
quote.text: How do Java and C# create cross-platform, portable programs, and why can't C++ do the same?

definitions.definition: (computing) Of a program: able to be copied directly from one machine to another without the use of an installer.

quote.citation: 2014, Bertrand Dufrasne, Bruce Allworth, Desire Brival, IBM XIV Storage System: Host Attachment and Interoperability, page 10:
quote.text: Starting with release 1.7, a portable version allows all Host Attachment Kit commands to be run without installing the Host Attachment Kit.

definitions.definition: A trailer or other movable structure used for classes at a school.
A portable building used for temporary purposes, particularly:

quote.text: A few portables, particularly the small laphelds, go one step further and come with software built into the computer.
Compaq portables have grown lighter and more powerful since then. Their newest luggable, the Compaq Portable III, is six times more powerful and 10 pounds lighter than the original model.

definitions.definition: (video games) A hand-held video gaming device.
